submissions.findingTextShort: An 8-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 52 mildly stressed/fatigued healthy adults reported selected stress, mood and sleep-quality signals with 400 mg/day L-ornithine.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial enrolled 52 mildly stressed or fatigued healthy Japanese adults and evaluated 400 mg/day L-ornithine for eight weeks. The study reported selected changes in cortisol/cortisol-to-DHEA-S, mood and sleep-quality measures. This small healthy-worker trial is a useful direct human anchor but does not independently justify the profile's current generic Grade B language or establish treatment efficacy for clinical anxiety or insomnia. Kirin-related industry affiliation/provenance must remain visible.
submissions.populationContext: Fifty-two mildly stressed/fatigued healthy Japanese adults, largely workers, in a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small sample, healthy-worker population and industry provenance limit generalization. Recompute grade only from governed claims rather than preserving the current unsupported Grade B string.

submissions.findingTextShort: A newer randomized trial found no saliva-cortisol improvement with 1,600 mg/day L-ornithine around an acute stress test, despite selected next-morning fatigue and anger-hostility improvements.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel trial in 65 healthy participants evaluated 1,600 mg/day L-ornithine for seven days plus acute dosing before the Trier Social Stress Test. Salivary cortisol was not improved, while selected next-morning fatigue-inertia and anger-hostility scores favored ornithine. The null cortisol result must remain first-class alongside the subjective signals. This acute-stress healthy-participant design does not establish treatment of anxiety or insomnia, and substantial Kirin industry affiliation/provenance must remain attached.
submissions.populationContext: Sixty-five healthy participants in a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled acute social-stress experiment.
submissions.usageContext: L-ornithine 1,600 mg/day for seven days plus acute pre-stress-test dosing.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Objective stress-hormone outcome was null while selected subjective next-morning outcomes improved; do not collapse this into a generic stress-reduction claim.
